## Overview

This is the final week of the R part of the course.
On Monday, after a brief introduction to **Bioconductor**,
a repository of R packages for omics data analysis,
we will analyze the RNA-seq gene counts produced by the nf-core rnaseq pipeline
in [week 11](../week11/w11c_nfcore2.qmd).
We will use the **DESeq2 package** to explore the data with a PCA,
and to identify differentially expressed genes.
We will visualize the results with a volcano plot, single-gene plots, and a heatmap.

On Wednesday, we will have a guest lecture.

## Before class: install packages

Installing the R packages for Monday's lecture can take 10--20 minutes,
so please do this **before class**:
start an RStudio Server session at OSC
([as in week 12](../week12/w12a_r-basics.qmd#starting-an-rstudio-server-session-at-osc)),
and run the following code in the R console:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages("BiocManager")
install.packages("pheatmap")
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "EnhancedVolcano"))
```
:::


## Lectures & Learning goals

Some of the things you will learn this week:

#### [RNA-seq count data analysis in R](./w15a_rnaseq.qmd)

- What Bioconductor is and how to install its packages
- Create a DESeq2 object that incorporates both the count data and the metadata
- Perform exploratory data analysis including a PCA
- Run a Differential Expression (DE) analysis
- Extract and visualize the DE results, including with a volcano plot and a heatmap
